source: segmentation (simulation footage, background replaced by white)
units: pixels (x right, y down) and seconds; no metric scale

camera.motion: static (no background; ball_middle stays within ~1 px while untouched, frames 0-27)
camera.perspective: none visible; 2D plane facing camera; all three balls have the same pixel diameter (~164 px)

description: Newton's-cradle-like setup: three equal grey spheres hanging (strings invisible) in a row. The left ball starts raised up-left, swings down along an arc and strikes the middle ball; the right ball is knocked out up-right along an arc, reaches its highest point at frame 54 and swings back. The middle ball barely moves (drifts ~10 px left and back); the left ball stops after impact, drifts ~16 px left and back.

bad_frames.1: segmentation failure: balls missing, only a stray half-dome blob at x 560-717, y 861-936; track centres in frame 1 are linear interpolation of frames 0 and 2 (bad_frame=1)

ball_left.path: circular arc, fitted pivot (645.0, 226.4), radius 558.9 px (frames 2-27, max residual 2.6 px)

ball_middle.describe: middle sphere, initially at (806.4, 792.3); is hit by ball_left
ball_middle.moves: almost static: x drifts from 806.5 to min 796.6 (frames ~51-55) and back to 805.1 at frame 79; y constant 792.3

ball_right.describe: rightmost sphere, initially at rest at (1311.8, 792.4); knocked out by the impact
ball_right.path: circular arc, fitted pivot (1308.7, 240.4), radius 552.4 px (frames 29-79, max residual 0.5 px)

static_objects: none (white background; strings, frame and ground are not rendered)
